clue.text: After circulating papers, sound preoccupied

indicators.note: After tells us the word for sound follows the turned papers
circulating suggests going round, so the word for papers is turned back to front

parts.note: ID is the usual abbreviation for identity papers
a sound is a narrow channel of sea, a strait

explanation.surface: Someone sounds distracted after handing out documents round a meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like a verb (to seem) but is the noun for a sea channel.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone distracted or absent-minded is preoccupied, the French-derived word for that state.

clue.text: Coercion, you, say, escaped from with revolting disguise

indicators.note: with joins the second piece after the first
escaped from says the letter sounding like you gets out of the coercion word

parts.note: duress is coercion by threats

indicators.note: say signals a word that sounds the same as the one spoken

parts.note: the letter U is pronounced like you
up as in up in arms, in revolt

explanation.surface: A kidnapper's coercion; you escape and disguise yourself in a revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'you, say' is the letter U, which leaves DURESS to give DRESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Phrasal verb: to dress up is to put on costume, i.e. to disguise oneself.

clue.text: Dupes flier we hear looking for bugs

definitions.meaning: a sap and a sucker are both gullible people, two dupes run together

definitions.text: flier we hear looking for bugs
definitions.meaning: a woodpecker heard tapping at bark as it hunts insects

explanation.walkthrough: 'Dupes' gives two words side by side, SAP and SUCKER. 'we hear' is not a homophone signal: we hear the bird drumming as it looks for bugs.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a sapsucker is a North American woodpecker, drilling bark for sap and insects.

clue.text: Remains on team holding United in second half

parts.note: re means on or concerning

indicators.note: holding means the team word contains the United letter
in second half places the letter in the latter part of the team word

parts.note: a side is a team
U is the abbreviation for United, as in team names

explanation.surface: A team stays ahead with Manchester United holding on in the second half of a match.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a residue is what remains after the rest has gone.

clue.text: Elected left-winger welcomes one piece of church music

parts.note: a candidate elected is in

indicators.note: welcomes means takes in, so the left-winger encloses the one

parts.note: Trot, short for Trotskyist, is a left-winger
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A newly elected socialist greets a choral item at a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an introit is a psalm or antiphon sung as the priest approaches the altar.

clue.text: Extremely minute number dropping ecstasy

indicators.note: dropping says a letter is let fall from the number word

parts.note: eighty is a number
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A tiny figure losing its drug content, as if reporting a minuscule quantity in a lab.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minute' reads as tiny but is the time unit, M; 'dropping' removes the E from EIGHTY.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal adverb: 'mighty fine' means very or extremely fine, chiefly in American usage.

clue.text: State of the old lady full of tensionafter breakdown

indicators.note: full of means the mother word is filled with the rearranged letters

parts.note: the old lady is slang for one's mother, ma

indicators.note: after breakdown says the word tension is broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: Mum's state of mind after a nervous breakdown, full of tension.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the old lady' is ma, slang for mother; 'State' is the definition, not a state of mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Minnesota is a Midwestern US state.

clue.text: Northern chap say will turn on soldiers before long

indicators.note: on in a down clue puts the first piece above the next
before puts the soldiers ahead of the word for long
will turn means the abbreviation for say is reversed

parts.note: e.g. means for example, say
OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers
to long for something is to be dying for it, to die

explanation.surface: A northern man will turn on the troops before long.
explanation.walkthrough: GEORDIE is a native of Newcastle upon Tyne in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a Geordie is a man from Tyneside in northern England.

clue.text: In never-ending race feel sorry for part of body

indicators.note: In signals the regret word goes inside the shortened race word
never-ending means the race word loses its final letter

parts.note: a tribe is a race or people
to rue is to regret or feel sorry for

explanation.surface: Pity for a body part during an endless race, like a runner's aching side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'never-ending' trims TRIBE to TRIB, which takes in RUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a true rib is one joined directly to the breastbone, part of the skeleton.

clue.text: Account for where something used to be

parts.note: ex- means former, what something used to be
where something is located is its position

explanation.surface: A request to explain the location of something now gone, as in a missing item.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'where something used to be' as a former position: an ex-position.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an exposition is a detailed explanation or account of a subject.

clue.text: Complains unofficially about limiting responsibility

indicators.note: about here means turned round, so the enclosed letters are read backwards
limiting means the letters are found bounded within the words complains unofficially

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles off the record about restrictions on what they are responsible for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'limiting' hides SUNO across the two words; 'about' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an onus is a burden or duty that falls on someone.

clue.text: No quarrels recollected with dead officer

indicators.note: recollected, read as re-collected, says the letters are gathered up again in a new order

explanation.surface: An officer is remembered as never having fallen out with anyone, now he has died.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recollected' rearranges the letters of NO QUARRELS and DEAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a squadron leader is a commissioned rank in the RAF, equivalent to a major.

clue.text: Smallest and narrowest central US state — one annoying person describes

indicators.note: describes in the sense of drawing around, so the annoying person encloses the state and the one

parts.note: an annoying person is a pest
OK is the postal abbreviation of Oklahoma, a state in the middle of the US
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A geography quiz asks for the smallest central US state, while an irritating person describes it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describes' means draws round, as a compass describes a circle. Pokey is informal British for small and cramped.
explanation.definitionFit: Superlative of pokey, informal British for cramped and small, as in a pokey little room.

clue.text: Resentful about sweet found in bits in hat

indicators.note: about means going round, so the resentful word encloses the scrambled sweet

parts.note: sour means bitter or resentful

indicators.note: found in bits says the word sweet is broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A grumpy person complains about finding sweet fragments in their hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweet' is anagram fodder, not a confection; the hat is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a sou'wester is a waterproof hat with a wide back brim, worn by sailors.

clue.text: Cops making visits

definitions.meaning: to cop is to get or obtain
to drop in on someone, calling briefly at their home

explanation.surface: Police officers paying calls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cops' is a verb, obtains, not police officers.
explanation.definitionFit: Phrasal verb with two senses: to obtain something, and to pay a casual call on someone.

clue.text: Subordinate position receives a command

indicators.note: receives means the location word takes in the next pieces

parts.note: a site is a position or location
to tell someone to do something is to command it

explanation.surface: A junior post is given an order from above.
explanation.definitionFit: Noun sense: a satellite is a dependent state or body subordinate to a more powerful one.

clue.text: Time in which uniform's no good for nurse

indicators.note: in which says the time word holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: an hour is a unit of time

indicators.note: no says the letter for good is absent from the clothing

parts.note: garb is clothing such as a uniform; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A period when wearing a uniform is no use for a nurse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uniform' is clothing, garb, and 'nurse' is a verb: to nurse a grudge.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb sense: to harbour a grudge or hope is to nurse it, holding it privately.

clue.text: Inform judge, ignoring second of answers

indicators.note: ignoring second of says the second instance of the answer letter is left out

parts.note: to appraise is to judge or assess
A is the abbreviation for answer

explanation.surface: Tell a judge to skip the second of the replies.
explanation.walkthrough: APPRAISE has two As; dropping the second leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to apprise someone of something is to tell or notify them.

clue.text: Platitude from bishop, I had seen visiting capital

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

indicators.note: visiting means going inside, so the contraction sits within the capital

parts.note: Rome is the Italian capital
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: A bishop's trite remark after a trip to the Vatican's city.
explanation.definitionFit: Figurative sense: a bromide, once a sedative, is a dull trite remark meant to soothe.

clue.text: Funny man's name withheld from criminal

indicators.note: withheld from says the letter for name is kept out of the criminal word

parts.note: a gangster is a criminal

explanation.surface: A comedian's identity is kept secret from a criminal.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a gagster tells gags, so is a comedian or joker.

clue.text: Cheat in America runs into present queen

indicators.note: into means the runs letter goes inside the present word

parts.note: a gift is a present
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: A US conman hurries in to give the Queen a gift.
explanation.definitionFit: American slang: a grifter is a swindler or con artist, someone who cheats people.

clue.text: Terribly polite word on The Weald, oddly enough

indicators.note: on in a down clue puts the first piece above the next

parts.note: gen is British slang for information, the word on something

indicators.note: oddly enough means take the odd-numbered letters of the phrase

explanation.surface: A very courteous remark on the Weald, oddly, as if from a rural guide.
explanation.walkthrough: THE WEALD, an area of south-east England, gives T, E, E, L from its odd letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Genteel means affectedly refined, so excessively or 'terribly' well-mannered and polite.

clue.text: Two boys getting extremely timely payment

parts.note: Roy and Al are two boys' names

indicators.note: extremely means take the extreme letters of timely, first and last

explanation.surface: Two lads receive money paid right on time.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a royalty is a payment made to an author or patent holder per sale.

clue.text: Supporter pursuing claim in expert fashion

indicators.note: pursuing means coming after, so the supporter follows the claim

parts.note: a profession is a declaration or claim, as in a profession of faith
an ally is a supporter

explanation.surface: A backer follows up a claim with professional competence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'claim' gives PROFESSION in the sense of an avowal, not a career.
explanation.definitionFit: Adverb for doing something with the skill of a trained practitioner, competently and expertly.

clue.text: One brief moment — almost rejected republic

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the combined pieces are read in reverse

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the word for a brief moment is lost

parts.note: a jiff, short for jiffy, is a brief moment

explanation.surface: A single fleeting instant is nearly turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: JIFF loses its last letter to JIF; I + JIF read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Fiji is a Pacific island nation that became a republic in 1987.

clue.text: Headline: "Drug given backing by policemen"

indicators.note: given backing read as sent backwards, so the drug word is reversed

parts.note: pot is slang for cannabis
The Bill is British slang for the police, also a long-running TV police drama

explanation.surface: A newspaper headline about a drug supported by police officers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Headline' is a verb here: to be the star act. THE BILL (Old Bill) is British slang for the police.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: to top the bill is to be the main performer advertised, i.e. to headline a show.

clue.text: Facing archdeacon, fellow appears powerless

parts.note: Ven, short for Venerable, is the title of an archdeacon

indicators.note: powerless says the letter for power is removed from the fellow word

parts.note: a peer is a fellow, an equal

explanation.surface: Up against a senior cleric, a colleague is seen to be helpless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'powerless' drops P (power) from PEER.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a veneer is a thin surface layer, or facing, applied over cheaper material.

clue.text: Turn, heading for exit, during boring comedy

indicators.note: during means the turn and first letter of exit come within the boring word

parts.note: dry means dull or boring
to roll is to turn over

indicators.note: heading for means take the first letter of exit

explanation.surface: A comic act's turn, making for the exit while a tedious comedy plays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn' suggests a stage act but is ROLL; E is the head of 'exit'.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: drollery is quaint humour, comical talk or behaviour.
